[PATH:theoretical] Analytical or computational modeling study comparing resilience metrics (e.g., size of largest connected component after failure) in random vs. disjoint-cycle network ensembles under simultaneous multi-node disturbances. — Provides formal mathematical or simulation-based confirmation of whether disjoint cycles inherently buffer against cascades, controlling for confounding factors like connectivity or degree distribution.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of empirical studies on real-world ecological networks (e.g., plant-pollinator, host-parasitoid, or food webs) that report network modularity or cycle structure and document responses to natural or experimental simultaneous disturbances. — Leverages existing data to test the hypothesis across diverse systems; can reveal whether disjoint cycles correlate with reduced cascading failures in natural contexts.
